newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks climb at open after Dow advance.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks climb at open after Dow advance.

text.p: Australian shares were marked higher at the open on Wednesday after the Dow industrials index soared more than two percent on Tuesday following weaker than expected March U.S. CPI data.
At 10.15 a.m (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 23.9 points at 2,405.6.
The June share price index was 35 points firmer at 2,398 and at a 7.6 point discount to the underlying index.
Early turnover was moderate but more active than in the past two days. Buying interest was focused on the five largest Australian companies and on the bank sector.

"We called the market up about 20 points this morning and it is already above that. There is no reason for the market to pull back later," said Stuart Smith, a senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Lance Jones.
Smith said he believed that most economists were happy with the fundamentals of the Australian share market.
The market's recent predictable behaviour in response to the Dow's fluctuations was also a reassuring factor, Smith said.
"Yesterday's volume wasn't worth writing about. I would like to see it do around A$800 million today but it doesn't look like doing that at this stage," he said.

Bank and media issues led the early charge with National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) the most active stock from the open. Dealers said it was the NAB's turn to be bought after the focus had been on Westpac Banking Corp and Commonwealth Bank of Australia stock in the past two sessions.
Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd ordinary and preferred stock was well-supported, as was Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Stocks were up across the board with rises outnumbering falls by a three to one ratio and about a third of issues traded remained steady.
